sections.title: Why We Use Fillers
sections.content: Filler words — 'um', 'uh', 'like', 'you know' — are verbal crutches. They occur when our brain is processing what to say next but our mouth keeps going. The pause feels uncomfortable, so we fill it with sound.
bullets: Fillers signal uncertainty and reduce your perceived authority
The pause that feels like an eternity to you is barely noticeable to the audience
Silent pauses project confidence; verbal fillers project nervousness

sections.title: The Replacement Strategy
sections.content: Instead of trying to eliminate fillers through willpower alone, practice the replacement strategy: when you feel the urge to say 'um', simply pause silently.
bullets: Step 1: Become aware — record yourself and count your fillers
Step 2: Catch the urge — notice when you are about to use a filler
Step 3: Replace — use a silent pause instead
Step 4: Practice — this gets easier with repetition

sections.title: With and Without Fillers
sections.content: Compare these two versions of the same statement:
sections.good: 'The evidence — (pause) — clearly shows that climate change is accelerating.'
sections.bad: 'Um, the evidence, like, clearly shows that, you know, climate change is basically accelerating.'
sections.explanation: The clean version is shorter, clearer, and sounds more confident.

sections.instruction: What is the most effective replacement for filler words?
options: Speaking faster so you have less time to use fillers
sections.feedback: A silent pause is the only replacement that eliminates fillers while actually improving your delivery.

sections.q: Why does a silent pause project more confidence than a filler word?
options: It makes you look like you forgot your lines
It signals that you are thinking deliberately rather than grasping for words
It is louder than a filler word
sections.explain: A deliberate pause signals composure and thoughtfulness. Fillers signal that your brain is racing to catch up with your mouth.

sections.statement: Using filler words occasionally is fine and does not affect how audiences perceive you.
sections.feedback: Research shows that even occasional filler words reduce perceived competence and credibility.

sections.sentence: The best replacement for filler words is a silent {0}.
sections.feedback: Replace the urge to say 'um' with a silent pause.

questions.q: What is the first step in the filler word replacement strategy?
options: Eliminate all pauses from your speech
Become aware by recording yourself and counting your fillers
questions.feedback: Awareness is the first step — you cannot fix what you do not notice.
